newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu dips against dollar in hectic trade.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu dips against dollar in hectic trade.

text.p: Romania's leu slid against the dollar on Thursday, closing at 7,400/500, compared with 7,200/260 a day earlier, as dollar demand surged after profit taking by foreign investors on equities markets, dealers said.

"There were some foreign investors who tried to change leu returns from equity trading into dollars," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Bucharest. "But I did not see orders to transfer that money abroad."

Both the bourse and the over-the-counter markets turned bearish this week after weeks of showing an upward trend. Brokers said investors saw opportunities for profit-taking as some stocks seemed now expensive.
Some traders said Thursday's quicker decline of the leu came as a correction after a relatively long flat period and was also fuelled by a recent downswing in money market rates.
But central bank (BNR) officials said they had expected the leu's slide following the greenback's strength in the international markets in recent days.
"Our market finally digested the recent moves of the U.S. currency on the international markets," BNR communication manager Adrian Vasilescu told Reuters, without elaborating.
Dealers said the local market was rather slow to react to international moves. "In theory, it might be true but our market is rather dictated by demand and supply here," said one.
Most traders were reluctant to say whether pressure on the leu would continue on Friday. "Such big (dollar buying) orders might be a temporary development," said another dealer.

The money market remained fairly liquid on Thursday with short-term rates hovering at about 15/20 percent amid smooth trading after the BNR mopped up some leu funds to prevent prices from falling further.
"The BNR was on the leu side taking deposits," said one trader with a state-run bank, adding that the BNR paid in a range of 25 to 30 percent.
The leu eased slightly against the dollar at retail shops, trading at 7,100/150 against 7,070/150 previously.
